questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, CMDB tables that previously required the itil role are now also accessible to which role?

options.text: sn_cmdb_admin
sn_cmdb_editor
cmdb_read
itil_admin

explanation.correct: Access to CMDB tables is no longer restricted to elevated roles: tables that required the itil role are now also accessible to the sn_cmdb_editor role. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes pair sn_cmdb_admin with tables that required the admin or itil_admin roles, not the itil role.
The release notes do not name cmdb_read for this change; they name sn_cmdb_editor.
itil_admin is one of the elevated roles that was previously required, not the new trimmed role.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

source.excerpt: CMDB tables that required the itil role are now also accessible to the sn_cmdb_editor user role.

questions.question: An instance is upgrading directly from Yokohama to the Australia release. What must an administrator do so that roles such as CMDB Admin and CMDB Editor are configured correctly?

options.text: Run the "Remove CMDB Roles from ITIL roles and Add CUD access to sn_cmdb_admin/sn_cmdb_editor roles" scheduled job
Manually add the itil role to the sn_cmdb_admin role
Activate the CMDB Workspace store app, which reassigns the roles automatically
Re-run the CMDB Health dashboard jobs after the upgrade

explanation.correct: When upgrading from Xanadu or Yokohama directly to Australia, the release notes require running the "Remove CMDB Roles from ITIL roles and Add CUD access to sn_cmdb_admin/sn_cmdb_editor roles" scheduled job to correctly configure roles such as CMDB Admin and CMDB Editor. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes do not call for adding itil to sn_cmdb_admin; the documented step is running a specific scheduled job.
The release notes do not describe CMDB Workspace as reassigning roles; the documented step is a scheduled job.
The release notes do not mention CMDB Health dashboard jobs for this task; they name a specific role-configuration scheduled job.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

documentation.section: Configuration Management Database (CMDB) - Important information for upgrading

source.excerpt: If you're upgrading from Xanadu or Yokohama directly to the Australia release, you must run the Remove CMDB Roles from ITIL roles and Add CUD access to sn_cmdb_admin/sn_cmdb_editor roles scheduled job to correctly configure some user roles, such as CMDB Admin and CMDB Editor.

questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, how is Dynamic IRE handled on zBooted instances compared with upgraded instances that use Static IRE?

options.text: Dynamic IRE is enabled by default on zBooted instances; upgraded instances using Static IRE can switch to Dynamic IRE
Dynamic IRE is enabled by default on upgraded instances; zBooted instances must activate it manually
Dynamic IRE is disabled on all instances until a plugin is activated
Upgraded instances are automatically and permanently converted from Static IRE to Dynamic IRE

explanation.correct: In Brazil, Dynamic IRE is enabled by default on zBooted instances, while upgraded instances that use Static IRE can switch to Dynamic IRE. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-configurationmanagementdatabasecmdb-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This reverses the documented behavior: zBooted instances get Dynamic IRE by default, and upgraded Static IRE instances can switch.
The release notes state Dynamic IRE is enabled by default on zBooted instances, so it is not disabled everywhere.
The release notes say upgraded instances using Static IRE can switch to Dynamic IRE, not that they are converted automatically.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

documentation.section: Configuration Management Database (CMDB) - Important information for upgrading

source.excerpt: Dynamic IRE is now enabled by default on zBooted instances, while on upgraded instances that are using Static IRE, you can switch into using Dynamic IRE.

glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode
glide.identification_engine.skip_duplicates
glide.cmdb.dedup.lookup_tables.enabled

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes tie glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode to OR operators in CMDB Query Builder V2 mode, not to lookup-table duplicates.
This property is not named in the release notes; the documented property is glide.identification_engine.lookup_match.create_duplicate_task_ci.enabled.
This property is not named in the release notes; the documented property is glide.identification_engine.lookup_match.create_duplicate_task_ci.enabled.

source.excerpt: Sort which duplicates do or don't require remediation by configuring the system property glide.identification_engine.lookup_match.create_duplicate_task_ci.enabled .

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, in CMDB Query Builder, a query uses OR operators and should run in V2 engine mode. Which system property must explicitly enable this?

options.text: glide.cmdb.query.v2_engine.enabled
glide.identification_engine.lookup_match.create_duplicate_task_ci.enabled
glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode
glide.cmdb.query_builder.allow_or

explanation.correct: Query structures not supported in V2 engine mode include OR operators unless explicitly enabled by the glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode system property. wrongAnswers.explanation: This property is not named in the release notes; OR support in V2 mode is controlled by glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode.

This property is not named in the release notes; the documented property is glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

source.excerpt: Query structures that aren't supported include related list conditions, NOT operators combined with filters, certain Service Mapping relationships, and OR operators unless explicitly enabled by the glide.cmdb.query.or_execution_mode system property.

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, which of the following tables now support domain separation on domain-separated instances? (Choose two.)

options.text: Key Value [cmdb_key_value]
Configuration Item [cmdb_ci]
Software Instance [cmdb_software_instance]
CI Relationship [cmdb_rel_ci]

wrongAnswers.explanation: cmdb_ci is not in the release notes' list of tables that gained domain separation support.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

source.excerpt: The following tables now support domain separation on instances which are configured with domain separation: Key Value [cmdb_key_value] Printer Instance [cmdb_print_queue_instance] Software Instance [cmdb_software_instance] Client Access [samp_client_access] Oracle Options [samp_oracle_options]

questions.question: Starting with the Brazil release, what happens when you reset a CMDB certification task?

options.text: All certification results return to a 'Review not completed' state and any added comments are removed
The task is closed and a new task is generated with the same CIs
Certification results are kept but the percent complete number resets to zero
Comments are kept and only failed certification results are reset

explanation.correct: Resetting a certification task restarts the certification process: all certification results return to 'Review not completed' and any added comments are removed. wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes describe resetting the existing task, not closing it and creating another.
The release notes say reset sets all certification results to 'Review not completed', so results are not kept.
The release notes say reset removes added comments and resets all results, not only failed ones.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Configuration Management Database (CMDB)

source.excerpt: Reset sets all certification results for the task to a 'Review not completed' state and removes any comments that were added.

questions.question: When configuring MID Server routing for Data Catalog metadata collectors, where does a connection run by default?

options.text: On the MID Server with the most available capacity
In the ServiceNow hosted cloud infrastructure
On a MID Server chosen by the collector owner at each run
On the data source host itself

When it runs on a MID Server, three routing models control how a MID Server is assigned to the collection job. wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes state the default is the ServiceNow hosted cloud infrastructure, not a MID Server.

The release notes offer only the hosted cloud infrastructure (the default) or a MID Server.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Data Catalog

Platform Analytics

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes name ServiceNow Vault for column classification; this plugin is not mentioned.
The release notes name ServiceNow Vault, not Platform Analytics, for column classification.
The release notes name ServiceNow Vault, not Instance Data Replication, for column classification.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Data Catalog

source.excerpt: Enable a metadata collector to classify harvested columns using ServiceNow Vault.

PIVOT
MERGE

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, an administrator edits a published data interface to add columns and swap a source table. What happens to existing consumers?

options.text: They are disconnected and must request access again
They keep using the interface and must reconnect to pick up the structural changes
They receive the structural changes automatically with no action
The edit is blocked until all consumers disconnect

explanation.correct: A published data interface can be modified (add columns, swap source tables, change the combination method, update mappings, or adjust join conditions). Existing consumers continue to use the interface and must reconnect to pick up structural changes. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-dataproducts-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say existing consumers continue to use the interface; they are not disconnected.
The release notes say consumers must reconnect to pick up structural changes.
The release notes describe editing a published interface while consumers continue to use it, not blocking the edit.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Data products

source.excerpt: Existing consumers continue to use the interface and must reconnect to pick up structural changes.

questions.question: Starting with the Australia release, the mssql-jdbc.7.4.1.jre8 jar file is no longer part of the MID Server distribution. What must an administrator with an MSSQL JDBC data source integration do?

options.text: Nothing; the MID Server downloads the jar automatically
Install this jar file or the vendor-recommended jar file
Switch the data source to a file-based import
Re-create the data source as a REST integration

explanation.correct: Because the mssql-jdbc.7.4.1.jre8 jar is no longer shipped with the MID Server, JDBC data source integrations that use it (any MSSQL connections) need this jar or the vendor-recommended jar installed, as described in KB0862383. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-importandexport-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The release notes say you must install the jar file yourself; they do not describe an automatic download.

The release notes call for installing the jar file, not re-creating the integration.

questions.question: According to the Australia release notes, what does Integration Hub Stream Producer do?

options.text: Imports Kafka messages into ServiceNow import sets on a schedule
Uses change data capture to stream inserts, updates, and deletes on selected ServiceNow tables to Kafka topics
Replicates ServiceNow tables to another instance through Instance Data Replication
Exports table data to Kafka as nightly batch files

explanation.correct: Stream Producer uses change data capture (CDC) to capture inserts, updates, and deletes on selected tables, formats them as messages, and sends them to a Kafka topic for real-time synchronization with external applications. See: https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/delta-zurich-brazil/brazil-zurich-integrationhub-release-notes.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: This reverses the direction: Stream Producer sends changes from ServiceNow tables to Kafka topics.
The release notes describe sending changes to Kafka topics, not Instance Data Replication.
The release notes describe CDC-based, real-time streaming, not nightly batch files.

references: Brazil delta release notes - Integration Hub

source.excerpt: Stream Producer uses change data capture (CDC) technology to capture inserts, updates, and deletes on selected tables. The captured changes are formatted as messages and sent to a Kafka topic, enabling real-time data synchronization with external applications.
